title: introduce-slateline-batch-lanes-and-hierarchical-quant-allocator
author: Nina Rodriguez
description: Motivation: Large fleets see varying request shapes; a single batching policy + flat quant profile leaves money on the table. This PR introduces 'SlateLine' batch lanes and a hierarchical quant allocator that together provide per-tenant/per-workload batch shaping and a priority-ranked quant fallback tree to reduce unit cost while respecting SLOs. Design summary: SlateLine divides the serving runtime batcher into lightweight lanes (fast-latency lane, balanced lane, throughput lane) with a tiny per-lane selector that uses recent shape histograms and token budget hints to pick the lane for each request. The hierarchical quant allocator maps model variants into a tree of quantization profiles: top nodes are high-fidelity (FP16/quant8-mixed) and leaves are aggressive int4/int2 variants. At runtime the allocator prefers higher-fidelity nodes but can step down along the tree when budget or capacity policies trigger. Key behaviors implemented: 1) lane selector service integrated into serving runtime (stable, lock-free sampling path), 2) lane-specific batching windows and kv-cache sharing limits, 3) quant allocator with soft budget quotas and graceful degradation path, 4) telemetry hooks for unit-econ attribution (tokens, lane, quant-level), 5) rollout flags and tenant override controls. Migration and safety: rollout gated by feature flag "slateline_enabled" per-cluster; default off. A conservative rollout profile named "slateline-conservative" is included which only enables lanes and allocator simulation (no quant fallbacks) to collect metrics for 24-72h. A second progressive profile enables live allocator step-downs with strict latency SLO enforcement and automatic revert if error or p95 latency regressions exceed thresholds. Testing: unit tests for allocator tree traversal, integration tests that run synthetic workloads exercising the three lanes, e2e perf test harness added to perf-canary to simulate tenant traffic and assert p50/p95 tail behavior and cost delta. CI: flaky integration test fixed by a deterministic seeding of the request sampler. Observability: new metrics: redwood.slateline.lane_chosen, redwood.slateline.quant_level, redwood.slateline.alloc_decisions, and taggable labels for unit_econ (tenant_id, route). Documentation: console docs and API playground snippets added under redwood-docs to explain flags and tenant override API. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-4312) - [x] unit+integration tests added - [x] perf harness entry for canary - [x] feature flags and rollout profiles - [x] telemetry and cost attribution hooks - [x] docs and CLI flag wiring Migration notes: Operators can test in simulation mode by enabling slateline_enabled=false and slateline_simulate=true; this will emit allocator decisions without altering quant levels. Live fallback thresholds are configurable via the console and via the cluster config file under runtime/batcher/slateline.yaml. Rollout plan: 1) enable simulation in canary region for 48h, 2) conservative flag in 2 small tenants for 72h, 3) progressive enable on low-risk tenants for 1 week, 4) full enable with automatic revert. Impact: internal perf-canary runs show roughly 7-12% token-cost reduction on mixed workloads with <2% p95 latency delta using conservative policies; aggressive policy hits 18-25% savings at cost of slightly higher p50/95 in synthetic throughput bursts. Related work: complements recent tenant-prefill and quant-profile recommendations; differs by pushing decision logic into the runtime and providing lane-aware batching rather than global batch windows. CI and post-merge tasks: tag release, update canary scenarios, watch the unit_econ dashboard and alert on cost regressions.

review_comments: Ethan Park: Can the lane selector decision be computed off the hot path? Nina: The selector is designed to be O(1) and uses a lock-free ring summary; heavy computation is done asynchronously and only compact hints are consulted on the hot path.
Priya Patel: Unit econ tags look great but we should ensure PIIs are not attached. Nina: Confirmed, tenant_id is hashed at ingestion in metrics_mapper; added a test asserting no raw ids emitted.

Marta Bloom: Suggest adding a guard to prevent int2 fallback for latency-sensitive lanes. Nina: Added an explicit lane->quant allowlist and updated slateline.yaml to include per-lane allowed_quant_levels.

Ethan Park: CI integration flake observed on scheduling test. Nina: Root cause was nondeterministic sampler; I fixed by seeding the sampler and reworked the test assertions to be tolerant to small jitter. CI now green.
ci_log_summary: Initial CI: 1 failing integration test (non-deterministic sampler). Fix applied and re-run. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, e2e perf dryrun).
release_notes: Introduce SlateLine batch lanes and hierarchical quant allocator to enable lane-aware batching and budgeted quant fallbacks. Rollout gated with conservative simulation mode. Expected cost reductions for mixed workloads while preserving latency SLOs. See slateline rollout guide in docs.
post_merge_actions: Create canary run ticket and attach perf-canary scenario
Notify SRE and cost-ops teams to watch unit_econ dashboards
Add slateline flags to operator upgrade notes
